plan.summary: Add append-only per-finding JSONL history and optional drift lookup, while keeping normal CLI output unchanged.

steps.action: Review and document a rollback plan for the new append-only security history log, including how to stop writes without altering existing records.
steps.rollback: switch log writes off and read existing records only
steps.observability: Rollback procedure approved; write-disable switch identified; no code changes yet.

steps.action: Publish the release note and notify users, support, and downstream stakeholders about the new persisted finding history and optional drift output.
steps.observability: Release note published; customer/support notices sent; escalation owner assigned; support briefed.

steps.action: Implement `adversarial-security-sim/history.py` with `verdict_drift(source, finding_id)` that reads append-only JSONL history and summarizes verdicts across runs.
steps.observability: Reader returns expected drift summaries on fixture logs; read-path error rate remains below threshold.

steps.action: Add append-only JSONL logging in `adversarial-security-sim/cli.py` at the end of each finding debate, storing source, finding_id, severity, verdict, hashes, model, and timestamp without full finding text.
steps.observability: Records append successfully; no plaintext bodies appear; write-path error rate stays under 0.1%; replication lag stays under 30s.

steps.action: Add and run append/read regression tests for the history writer and verdict_drift helper, including privacy checks for hashed outputs only.
steps.gate: wait_for:CI green on add/read/append regression suite
steps.observability: CI passes on append, read, drift-summary, and privacy assertions.

steps.action: Integrate optional `--show-drift` into the CLI so drift summary prints before the report only when explicitly requested, leaving default output unchanged.
steps.rollback: turn off the feature flag and redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Default report output is unchanged; `--show-drift` prints only the drift summary; no extra output in normal runs.

steps.action: Stage the rollout in an approved window outside business hours, launch windows, major events, incidents, and Friday afternoon, with log writes enabled only after readiness gates pass.
steps.rollback: Defer deployment and keep using the current storage layout
steps.observability: Deployment timing is compliant; no business-hours storage-layout change; rollout stays within approved window.

steps.action: Enable production writes and `--show-drift` behind the release gates, while monitoring write error rate, drift read error rate, replication lag, and CLI output stability.
steps.rollback: disable --show-drift and stop appending new JSONL records
steps.observability: Write-path and read-path error rates remain below 0.1%; replication lag stays under 30s; normal CLI output remains unchanged.

steps.action: If historical records need initial population, backfill in small batches into the JSONL log without rewriting existing entries.
steps.rollback: Pause backfill jobs and resume with smaller batches
steps.observability: IOPS stays within baseline+20%; append-only invariant holds; no replication-lag spikes.

steps.action: Plan the future SQLite memory-backend migration path so the JSONL history can be dual-written during cutover, but keep the current JSONL store as the active path until the backend is live and reviewed.
steps.rollback: Keep writing to current JSONL store; defer migration
steps.observability: Migration remains deferred until the SQLite write path is live; no storage-layout change is introduced prematurely.

conflicts.issue: Multiple blockers require approvals, timing windows, and release-note/user-notice prerequisites before drift becomes visible. Resolved by sequencing reader, rollout comms, and approvals before enabling `--show-drift`; normal CLI output stays unchanged unless the flag is used.

History must be append-only and privacy-preserving, while future backend migration may change storage. Resolved by keeping JSONL as the active append-only log now and deferring any SQLite move until the backend write path is live and compliance-reviewed.
